tagline: The World's Most Beautiful Freeway, by its own sign.
intro: South of San Bruno, Interstate 280 leaves the cities to the bay side and keeps to the Peninsula hills, the Santa Cruz Mountains to the west and now and then San Francisco Bay to the east. Much of the way it runs just inside the eastern rim of the San Andreas rift valley. From Hillsborough to Belmont it looks over Crystal Springs Reservoir, which partly fills the rift with water piped more than 160 miles from Hetch Hetchy.
It was dedicated in the 1960s as the Junipero Serra Freeway, and a dedication sign up in Daly City still calls it the World's Most Beautiful Freeway.

moments.title: Crystal Springs Rest Area
moments.text: Off the northbound lanes. From 1975 a 26-foot faux-sandstone Junípero Serra stood here, visible both ways; Caltrans took him down in 2025, citing graffiti and its art program's rules.

moments.title: Doran Memorial Bridge
moments.text: Twin steel girder bridges carry the freeway high over San Mateo Creek. Before they opened in 1969, more than 30,000 people walked across on Pedestrian Day.

moments.title: Ladera
moments.text: Ladera is Spanish for hillside. The land was once a ranch where the Macdonoughs bred racehorses, Ormonde among them, a stud that had raced in England and never lost.
